item.title: El Chernóbil asturiano: el pueblo abandonado ubicado junto a una antigua central térmica que tiene cine, escuela, club social y hasta consultorio médico
item.description: Había una vez un pueblo con cine, escuela, club social, piscina y hasta un consultorio médico de rigor. Solo que está abandonado. No es un cuento, existe, está en Tineo (Asturias) y se llama Soto de la Barca. Algunos apodan a este lugar el “Chernóbil asturiano”, aunque aquí nunca hubo un reactor nuclear. Prípiat tuvos plazos y 49.000 evacuados. Soto no recibió ni la alerta de la sirena: se vació a cámara lenta, nómina a nómina. item.title: Dogmatic Nordic liberals v eastern family values: culture-clash drama Fjord touches nerves in Norway and Romania
item.description: Cristian Mungiu’s Cannes winner echoes the news story of a Romanian couple whose children were taken by the Norwegian government. As it heads to London film festival, two writers explain how the film exposes real hypocrisies When Cristian Mungiu’s Fjord was shown in Romania as a one-day preview this June, the reception was extraordinary. Across 53 towns and 96 cinemas, the film reportedly pulled in over 40,000 viewers in a single night, a number arthouse cinema rarely sees in Romania. But the response here had little to do with cinema. It felt instead like a reopening of a familiar fault line… Fuente: The Guardian - Culture.

item.title: Make Me Well by Xand van Tulleken – an eye-opening takedown of wellness myths
item.description: The engaging TV doctor dismantles the spurious science behind modern day snake oils, from collagen to turmeric When Xand van Tulleken set off on a journey into the wild west of wellness, he didn’t expect to discover anything new about vitamin D. item.title: Australia hands Ming dynasty Buddha back to China amid ongoing mystery over its arrival
item.description: A 500-year-old Buddha statue that was found buried by a roadside in Australia has been returned to China, leaving an ongoing mystery about how it arrived in the country. The 15cm (six-inch) bronze figurine was formally handed over to Chinese consular representatives during a ceremony in the coastal town of Denham in Shark Bay on Tuesday, the public broadcaster ABC reported.
